Instrument / source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 — Artificial Intelligence Act
Legal status: Enacted; consolidated text listed by AI Act Explorer as amended through 27 Jul 2026
Effective / application date: Phased application; check current consolidated text and transitional provisions
Authority: European Parliament and Council / European Commission
Applicability to AI agents: Applies to AI systems within territorial and material scope; agent status alone does not automatically determine risk class. Classify by intended purpose and Annex III / product safety routes.
Financial-market relevance: Creditworthiness and credit scoring of natural persons can be high-risk under Annex III; trading agents are not automatically high-risk solely because they trade.
Key obligations / findings: Risk management, data governance, technical documentation, logging, transparency, human oversight, accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity, post-market monitoring and enforcement.
Security failure themes: Unsafe autonomy; insufficient oversight; weak logging; data poisoning; cybersecurity; opaque decisions
Verification note: Use official consolidated text and verify the amendment (Digital Omnibus) and transitional dates before making article-level claims.

Instrument / source: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 — Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA)
Legal status: Enacted and applicable
Authority: European Parliament and Council / European Supervisory Authorities
Applicability to AI agents: Applies to in-scope financial entities and relevant ICT third-party arrangements; AI model/cloud/tool providers may be captured as ICT dependencies depending on service and contract.
Financial-market relevance: Directly relevant to banks, investment firms, payment institutions, market infrastructures and other in-scope financial entities.
Key obligations / findings: ICT risk management; incident classification/reporting; resilience testing; ICT third-party risk; contractual controls; oversight of critical ICT third-party providers.
Security failure themes: Agent/tool outage; compromised model provider; cloud concentration; supply-chain compromise; data breach; service disruption
Verification note: ESMA confirms applicability from 17 Jan 2025 and describes risk management, testing, incidents, information sharing and third-party oversight.

Instrument / source: Directive 2014/65/EU (MiFID II), Article 17 — Algorithmic trading
Legal status: In force; national implementation applies
Effective / application date: 2018-01-03 (MiFID II application date; confirm local transposition)
Authority: European Parliament and Council / national competent authorities
Applicability to AI agents: Technology-neutral: can apply where an AI agent is used in a regulated investment firm’s algorithmic trading activity.
Financial-market relevance: Directly relevant to algorithmic execution, market access, high-frequency trading and market-making strategies.
Key obligations / findings: Effective systems and risk controls; resilience and capacity; trading thresholds and limits; prevention of erroneous orders/disorderly markets; testing, monitoring, business continuity and records.
Security failure themes: Erroneous orders; runaway trading; unauthorized strategy changes; market disorder; weak auditability
Verification note: ESMA Interactive Single Rulebook text reviewed. Article 17(1), (2) and (6) are especially relevant; RTS 6 should be separately registered and analyzed.

Instrument / source: MAS Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence Risk Management for Financial Institutions
Legal status: Published; supervisory expectations; not a statute
Authority: Monetary Authority of Singapore
Applicability to AI agents: Applies to all financial institutions in scope and all forms of AI technologies; proportionate to risk profile and scale/nature of use.
Financial-market relevance: Directly addresses AI use across regulated financial institutions.
Key obligations / findings: AI governance and risk management expectations across AI lifecycle; details to be extracted from official guideline PDF before article/paragraph-level coding.
Security failure themes: Autonomy; model risk; governance gaps; human oversight; cyber/ICT risk; third-party AI risk
Verification note: MAS page states published 7 Oct 2026 and effective 7 Oct 2027. Do not label as legislation. Obtain and review linked PDF for precise paragraph mapping.

Instrument / source: FSB — Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence (Final Report)
Legal status: Final report; non-binding sound practices
Authority: Financial Stability Board
Applicability to AI agents: Explicitly discusses agentic AI and AI adoption in financial institutions; practices are encouraged and tailored to context.
Financial-market relevance: Directly relevant to financial institutions, systemic resilience and supervisory coordination.
Key obligations / findings: 12 practices: strategic oversight; governance/accountability; risk frameworks/documentation; adaptability; materiality assessment; model selection; data governance; explainability; performance management; human oversight; cyber/ICT risk; third-party AI risk.
Security failure themes: Insufficient oversight; poor data quality; cyber compromise; third-party concentration; performance drift; opaque agent decisions
Verification note: Official FSB final report dated 15 Oct 2026. Strong priority source for agentic AI in financial services.

Instrument / source: NIST AI 600-1 — Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
Legal status: Voluntary; not a binding regulation
Authority: US National Institute of Standards and Technology
Applicability to AI agents: Applies as a voluntary risk-management reference to generative AI systems; agent-specific applicability depends on implementation.
Financial-market relevance: Useful for financial institutions designing/testing generative AI components and agent interfaces.
Key obligations / findings: Generative AI risk taxonomy and suggested actions aligned to AI RMF functions; supports governance, mapping, measurement and management.
Security failure themes: Prompt injection-related risks (where addressed by profile), confabulation, data privacy, information security, harmful bias, supply-chain and evaluation risks
Verification note: NIST publication page identifies report number AI 600-1 and describes intended voluntary use; review full PDF before attributing a specific control to a section.

Instrument / source: Regulation (EU) No 596/2014 — Market Abuse Regulation (MAR)
Legal status: Enacted; in force (subject to amendments/consolidation checks)
Authority: European Parliament and Council / ESMA / national competent authorities
Applicability to AI agents: Technology-neutral; applies to conduct involving financial instruments in scope, including conduct mediated by AI agents.
Financial-market relevance: Directly relevant to agent-enabled trading, order placement, market manipulation, insider dealing and unlawful disclosure.
Key obligations / findings: Article 12 defines market manipulation; Article 15 prohibits market manipulation; Article 14 prohibits insider dealing and unlawful disclosure. Algorithmic execution does not displace responsibility under MAR.
Security failure themes: Agent-driven spoofing/layering; manipulative order patterns; misuse of inside information; coordinated agent behaviour
Verification note: Primary law. Agent applicability is functional, not AI-specific. Verify latest consolidated version and national enforcement practice.

Instrument / source: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 — General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
Legal status: Enacted; applicable since 2018-05-25
Authority: European Parliament and Council / national data protection authorities / EDPB
Applicability to AI agents: Applies where an agent processes personal data within territorial scope; Article 22 is narrower than all AI-assisted decisions.
Financial-market relevance: Relevant to credit decisions, customer profiling, fraud detection, financial advice and agent access to customer data.
Key obligations / findings: Articles 5 (principles), 6 (lawfulness), 22 (solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, subject to conditions/exceptions), 25 (data protection by design), 32 (security), 35 (DPIA).
Security failure themes: Personal-data leakage; unauthorized profiling; discriminatory automated decisions; insecure agent memory or logs
Verification note: Do not imply Article 22 covers every AI-assisted decision: it concerns decisions based solely on automated processing with legal or similarly significant effects, subject to statutory conditions.

Instrument / source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/589 — RTS 6
Legal status: Enacted; in force; complements MiFID II Article 17
Authority: European Commission / ESMA / national competent authorities
Applicability to AI agents: Applies to investment firms engaged in algorithmic trading; can cover AI agents when they form part of the trading algorithm or related systems.
Financial-market relevance: Direct: algorithm development, testing, deployment, monitoring, kill functionality, limits and governance.
Key obligations / findings: Technical requirements for algorithmic trading systems, development/testing, deployment controls, real-time monitoring, business continuity, capacity, thresholds and emergency cancellation/kill functionality; map exact provisions before clause-level legal opinion.
Security failure themes: Runaway trading; rogue strategy deployment; defective kill switch; untested model updates; erroneous orders
Verification note: Register separately from MiFID II Article 17. Exact article mapping and amendments should be extracted from the official consolidated legal text.

Instrument / source: Directive (EU) 2015/2366 — Payment Services Directive 2 (PSD2)
Legal status: Enacted; national transposition applies; review current amendments and payment package transition
Authority: European Parliament and Council / EBA / national competent authorities
Applicability to AI agents: Technology-neutral; relevant where an agent initiates, authenticates, routes or manages payment transactions or accesses payment accounts.
Financial-market relevance: Direct relevance to agent-initiated payments, account information, payment initiation and strong customer authentication.
Key obligations / findings: Payment-service authorization and conduct requirements; security and incident obligations; strong customer authentication and secure communication under applicable PSD2 provisions and RTS; assess current legislative transition to PSD3/PSR.
Security failure themes: Unauthorized agent payments; credential misuse; payment fraud; compromised API access; transaction replay
Verification note: PSD2 is being replaced/modernized through EU payment-services reforms. Confirm current transitional status before relying on it for a 2026 deployment.

Instrument / source: SEC Exchange Act Rule 15c3-5 — Market Access Rule
Legal status: Final rule; in force
Authority: US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
Applicability to AI agents: Applies to broker-dealers with market access, including sponsored/direct electronic access; relevant if AI agent submits orders through covered access arrangements.
Financial-market relevance: Direct relevance to order controls, pre-trade risk controls and broker-dealer supervisory responsibility.
Key obligations / findings: Requires documented risk-management controls and supervisory procedures reasonably designed to limit financial exposure, enforce regulatory requirements, prevent orders exceeding preset credit/capital thresholds or appearing erroneous, and restrict access to authorized persons.
Security failure themes: Unauthorized orders; excess exposure; runaway trading; bypassed pre-trade controls; agent credential misuse
Verification note: Official SEC final-rule page. Rule applies to broker-dealers, not every trader or software vendor. Analyse current rule text and interpretive guidance.

Instrument / source: SEC Regulation Systems Compliance and Integrity (Regulation SCI)
Legal status: Enacted; in force; applies only to SCI entities
Authority: US Securities and Exchange Commission
Applicability to AI agents: AI agent relevance is indirect: applies when AI systems form part of systems operated by covered SCI entities or their critical systems.
Financial-market relevance: Market infrastructure, exchanges, clearing agencies, certain alternative trading systems and plan processors.
Key obligations / findings: Requires policies/procedures for capacity, integrity, resiliency, availability and security of SCI systems; incident notification, business continuity and testing obligations under the rule.
Security failure themes: Agent compromise affecting exchange systems; service disruption; integrity failure; cascading market infrastructure outage
Verification note: Scope is entity-specific. Do not generalize Regulation SCI to all financial institutions or AI vendors.

Instrument / source: Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA) and FTC Safeguards Rule (16 CFR Part 314)
Legal status: Enacted; Safeguards Rule in force with amended requirements
Authority: US Congress / FTC and relevant financial regulators
Applicability to AI agents: Applies to covered financial institutions and customer information; AI agent vendors/processors may be relevant as service providers under contractual and oversight duties.
Financial-market relevance: Relevant to financial customer information handled by agents, model providers and outsourced AI services.
Key obligations / findings: Privacy and safeguarding obligations; written information security program; risk assessment; access controls; encryption; monitoring; service-provider oversight; incident response and reporting under applicable provisions.
Security failure themes: Customer data exfiltration; agent over-privilege; insecure vendor integration; confidential financial data leakage
Verification note: GLBA coverage and regulator differ by institution type. FTC Safeguards Rule is not the sole GLBA implementation for all regulated entities.

Instrument / source: FCA — AI and the FCA: our approach
Legal status: Current FCA policy approach; not a standalone AI statute or new AI rule
Authority: Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)
Applicability to AI agents: Relevant to firms using AI, including agentic applications, under existing FCA rules and principles.
Financial-market relevance: Directly relevant to regulated UK financial firms and markets.
Key obligations / findings: FCA states it intends to rely on existing frameworks rather than introduce additional AI-specific regulation; existing obligations remain applicable, including governance, consumer outcomes, operational resilience, systems and controls.
Security failure themes: Unclear accountability; inadequate monitoring; consumer harm; poor model governance; third-party risks
Strictness tier (indicative): 2 — supervisory policy relying on existing binding rules
Verification note: Important counterexample to the EU's horizontal AI Act: do not label the FCA approach a dedicated AI law.

Instrument / source: OSFI Guideline E-23 — Model Risk Management
Legal status: Final guideline published; future effective date 2027-05-01
Authority: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI)
Applicability to AI agents: Applies to federally regulated financial institutions; explicitly addresses AI/ML and notes possible prevalence of dynamic self-learning and autonomous decision-making models.
Financial-market relevance: Direct relevance to bank and insurer model risk, including AI used in decisions and operations.
Key obligations / findings: Enterprise-wide model risk management expectations; model inventory, governance, development, validation, use, monitoring and controls under risk-based approach. Detailed paragraph-level mapping required.
Security failure themes: Model drift; autonomous decision error; flawed validation; opacity; model concentration and operational loss
Verification note: OSFI identifies AI/ML and autonomous decision-making in its overview. Guideline effective 1 May 2027; not yet effective on 29 Oct 2026.

Instrument / source: Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and the Creation of a Foundation for Trust (AI Basic Act)
Legal status: Enacted; effective 2026-01-22; amended 2026-01-20 with amended text effective 2026-07-21
Authority: National Assembly / Ministry of Science and ICT
Applicability to AI agents: Broad AI system definition includes varying autonomy and adaptability; agent coverage depends on system and statutory scope.
Financial-market relevance: Potential relevance to financial services; determine whether specific financial use cases meet high-impact AI sector and statutory criteria.
Key obligations / findings: Framework governance; high-impact AI and generative AI obligations; safety, transparency, notification and government oversight. Need current English/Korean text and Enforcement Decree for exact articles and scope.
Security failure themes: High-impact decision risk; insufficient transparency; safety failures; governance and accountability gaps
Verification note: Use amended official Korean legal text and Enforcement Decree. Financial-sector classification must be verified rather than presumed.

Instrument / source: Act on Promotion of Research and Development, and Utilization of Artificial Intelligence-related Technology (Act No. 53 of 2025)
Legal status: Enacted; fully in force from 2025-09-01
Authority: Japanese Diet / Cabinet Office / AI Strategic Headquarters
Applicability to AI agents: Broadly covers AI-related technology; establishes promotion and coordination mechanisms rather than EU-style detailed provider/deployer compliance duties.
Financial-market relevance: Relevant as national AI policy context for Japanese financial institutions; financial rules remain central.
Key obligations / findings: Basic principles, national AI strategy, strategic headquarters and government measures. Avoid treating it as a comprehensive risk-classification or agent-specific obligations statute.
Security failure themes: Governance fragmentation; policy-level gaps; reliance on sectoral financial/cyber laws
Strictness tier (indicative): 2 — binding promotion framework, relatively light direct operator duties
Verification note: Official Cabinet Office page says promulgated 4 Jun 2025 and fully in force 1 Sep 2025. Do not overstate prescriptive obligations.

Instrument / source: Implementation Opinions on Standardized Application and Innovative Development of AI Agents (智能体规范应用与创新发展实施意见)
Legal status: Official policy document published; not classified here as a statute or standalone administrative regulation
Effective / application date: 2026-05-08 (policy publication; legal effect requires legal analysis)
Authority: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC), NDRC and MIIT
Applicability to AI agents: Explicitly defines AI agents as systems with autonomous perception, memory, decision-making, interaction and execution.
Financial-market relevance: Potentially relevant to financial use cases among 19 broad application scenarios; not a finance-specific rule.
Key obligations / findings: Calls for safety and controllability, standards/protocols, security, application-driven development and orderly governance. Map each directive and issuing authority before treating as enforceable duty.
Security failure themes: Agent goal hijacking; unsafe execution; tool abuse; identity/permission failures; systemic deployment risk
Verification note: Primary official CAC publication. The State Council portal summary confirms joint issuing bodies and agent definition. Determine legal status and mandatory force provision by provision.

Instrument / source: Interim Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services
Legal status: In force; applies to covered public-facing generative AI services in mainland China
Authority: CAC and other relevant Chinese authorities
Applicability to AI agents: May apply to agentic services if they constitute covered generative AI services provided to the public in mainland China; scope must be tested.
Financial-market relevance: Relevant to public-facing financial AI assistants or agents, subject to financial-sector and data rules.
Key obligations / findings: Provider responsibilities, training-data and personal-information requirements, content controls, security assessment/filing requirements in applicable cases, and service-user protections.
Security failure themes: Unsafe generated instructions; harmful outputs; data misuse; service security; failure to respond to complaints
Verification note: Do not assume all internal enterprise agents are in scope; analyze the service definition and exceptions.

Instrument / source: Provisions on the Administration of Algorithmic Recommendations in Internet Information Services
Legal status: In force
Authority: CAC and other relevant authorities
Applicability to AI agents: Potentially applies to algorithmic recommendation services; not every autonomous agent is an algorithmic recommendation service.
Financial-market relevance: Relevant to financial platforms recommending products, feeds or personalized financial content; application depends on service design.
Key obligations / findings: Algorithmic recommendation governance, user rights, transparency, prohibited uses, filing/security assessment for specified services and provider responsibilities.
Security failure themes: Manipulative personalization; opaque recommendations; discriminatory targeting; algorithmic amplification
Verification note: Classify by service function, not by use of an AI agent label. Check official Chinese text for exact clauses.

Instrument / source: Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL)
Legal status: Enacted; in force
Authority: National People's Congress Standing Committee / CAC and other authorities
Applicability to AI agents: Applies to processing personal information by agents and their providers within territorial/extraterritorial scope.
Financial-market relevance: Relevant to credit, payments, wealth management, identity verification, fraud detection and customer-facing agents.
Key obligations / findings: Article 24 on automated decision-making (transparency, fairness, non-discrimination and certain rights); Article 51 security measures; Article 55 personal information protection impact assessment in specified cases; cross-border transfer rules.
Security failure themes: Automated discriminatory decisions; profiling; data leakage; insecure memory and cross-border data flows
Verification note: Use official statute and authoritative translation. Article 24 is especially relevant; distinguish from GDPR Article 22.

Instrument / source: Data Security Law
Legal status: Enacted; in force
Authority: National People's Congress Standing Committee / relevant sectoral authorities
Applicability to AI agents: Applies to data processing activities within scope; agent data pipelines, logs, training and inference data may be covered.
Financial-market relevance: Relevant to financial data, important data, cross-border processing and data security governance.
Key obligations / findings: Data classification and grading, risk monitoring, security management, incident response and important-data controls under applicable provisions.
Security failure themes: Data exfiltration; corruption; loss of integrity; cross-border data risks; operational disruption
Verification note: Applicability depends on data category, operator and sector-specific rules; map exact obligations before assigning an entity duty.

Instrument / source: Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China
Legal status: Enacted; in force; amendments and current consolidated text must be checked
Authority: National People's Congress Standing Committee / CAC and sectoral authorities
Applicability to AI agents: Applies to network operators and covered network operations; agent-hosting platforms and financial infrastructure may fall within scope.
Financial-market relevance: Relevant to network security, critical information infrastructure and financial digital services.
Key obligations / findings: Network security obligations, security protection systems, incident response, data protection and critical information infrastructure requirements where applicable.
Security failure themes: Compromised agent infrastructure; service outage; unauthorized access; critical infrastructure disruption
Verification note: Verify subsequent amendments and implementing rules, including current effective text, before legal conclusions.

Instrument / source: Bill PL 2338/2023 — Artificial Intelligence Legal Framework
Legal status: Not enacted as of latest official legislative status located; bill advanced through legislative process and remains under Chamber consideration
Authority: Federal Senate / Chamber of Deputies
Applicability to AI agents: Would establish risk-based obligations for AI systems, including potential financial-sector applications, if enacted in final form.
Financial-market relevance: Potentially relevant to credit, financial services and high-risk AI; current law remains applicable independently.
Key obligations / findings: Proposed risk classification, rights, governance, liability and oversight provisions. Do not enter proposed clauses as current duties.
Security failure themes: Regulatory gap; uncertainty; inconsistent accountability
Verification note: Official Chamber status shows legislative processing and related bills through Sep 2026. Recheck live status before each update; Senate passage alone did not enact it.

Instrument / source: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications / Agent Control Standard (2026 resources)
Legal status: Community-developed security guidance; not legislation; verify final release/version and governance status
Authority: OWASP GenAI Security Project
Applicability to AI agents: Explicitly addresses agentic AI application security, including agent goals, tools, identity, memory and execution.
Financial-market relevance: Useful technical control catalogue for agents deployed in banking, payments, trading and financial operations.
Key obligations / findings: Agent-specific threat taxonomy and control guidance; map agent goal hijack, tool misuse, identity/privilege abuse and memory/context poisoning to financial controls.
Security failure themes: Prompt injection; tool misuse; excessive agency; identity abuse; memory poisoning; unauthorized execution
Verification note: OWASP is a recognized community security project, not a regulator. Treat as technical evidence, not legal authority. Verify the exact Agent Control Standard version before citing clauses.

Instrument / source: MITRE ATLAS — Adversarial Threat Landscape for AI Systems
Legal status: Living knowledge base; non-binding
Authority: MITRE
Applicability to AI agents: Explicitly includes generative and agentic AI threat techniques and empirical case studies.
Financial-market relevance: Useful for mapping attacks against financial AI agents and infrastructure; not a financial regulation.
Key obligations / findings: Adversary tactics, techniques, mitigations and case studies for AI-enabled systems; supports threat modelling and control mapping.
Security failure themes: Prompt injection; model compromise; credential theft; privilege escalation; exfiltration; agentic abuse
Verification note: Technical threat taxonomy; distinguish demonstrated/realized incidents from feasible techniques. Record case-study evidence separately.
